transcript: If you're looking to clear your sinuses, just go see ragtime at Lincoln Center — you will cry. You'll also get to experience one of the most beautiful scores of the American theater, performed to the nines by an all-star cast and a magnificent orchestra. Set at the turn of the 20th century, this is a story about three different communities all trying to live a version of the American dream. This production is a slightly beefed up version of the run at City Center last Fall, but in many ways it remains artfully modest. The script and the score are at the forefront and the mostly identical cast is just as glorious as before. Everyone is excellent including Caissie Levy and Brandon Uranowitz, but I was especially impressed by Nichelle Lewis and Ben Levi Ross in their supporting roles. Everyone is a gem in this production, but really, Joshua Henry and his golden pipes are the crown jewel. His career-defining performance here is truly one for the ages, and they might as well start engraving and polishing his Tony Award now. If you didn't catch this at City Center or if you're not familiar with the show, do not let this one pass you by. It's a classic for a reason, though it's not perfect — it's long and almost overwhelmingly wide in scope, and it falls into some tropes that haven't necessarily aged well. That said, I still think it's an important artifact for the time it portrays and the time it was written in, over 25 years ago — and still, so much of it rings true today. Material aside, I cannot overstate how good this production is — it honestly ascended me. Ragtime is running at the Vivian Beaumont through the end of the year, don't miss it. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
classificationReason: Creator clearly saw Ragtime at Lincoln Center and provides detailed review of cast, orchestra, and emotional impact
